news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: The Sensex plummeted by 1,000 points and the Nifty 50 index breached the critical 23,000 psychological support level within the last 48 hours.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail investors view this as a systemic collapse or a 'black swan' event, leading to panic selling at the bottom to prevent further losses.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: This is a classic 'liquidity sweep' where institutional algorithms trigger stop-loss clusters below the 23,000 level to accumulate high-quality assets at a discount from retail hands before a potential mean reversion.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Never place stop-losses at round psychological numbers; use volatility-adjusted ATR (Average True Range) buffers to avoid being hunted by institutional liquidity sweeps.

slides.title: Liquidity sweep epdi nadakudhu?
slides.card_text: 1. Retailers ellarum 23,000-la stop-loss veipanga. 2. Algorithms indha round number-a target panni price-a keezha thallum. 3. Retailers panic-la sell panna, institutions adhai discount-la vanguvanga.

slides.title: Capital extraction-oda hidden math
slides.card_text: Neenga 1 lakh invest panni 8% drop aagum bodhu, adhu 92k aagudhu. Panic aagi exit aagum bodhu, unga loss confirm aagudhu. Institutional algorithms unga 'stop-loss' orders-a fuel-a use panni market-a reverse panranga.

slides.title: Golden rule to protect capital
slides.card_text: Round psychological numbers-la (23,000, 22,500) stop-loss veikkadheenga. Adhukku badhila, ATR (Average True Range) buffer use pannunga. Idhu unga trade-a institutional liquidity sweeps-la irundhu safe-a vachukudum.
